expectation: VISTA should be a membranous/cytoplasmic stain on a subset of myeloid (CD14+) cells and T cells, scattered as single cells in stroma and tumour, and on some tumour cells. It should be a minority population of discrete cell-sized rings or blobs.
observed: A: yellow is widespread haze in most ROIs, with a few saturated blobs and fibre-like streaks. B/C: sparse small specks with no clear clustering. D: the brightest cell is a long linear fibre or stripe, not a cell. E: cell-sized VISTA blobs, some white overlap with CD14, but much green sits on CD14-negative tissue.
why: There is some cell-scale VISTA signal with partial CD14 overlap, but it sits on diffuse haze and fibre-like artefacts, so contrast is low and specificity is only partial.
